whatItIs.text: A morning-glory relative grown for its starchy, sweet root — unrelated to potatoes beyond plant-order cousins, and in parts of North America confusingly sold as 'yams'.

historyNote.text: The sweet potato is native to tropical South America in modern Ecuador; it is the only crop plant of major importance in its whole 1,000-species family, and its leaves are eaten as greens with a nutritional profile comparable to spinach.

howToChoose.text: Choose firm, heavy tubers without cracks or soft spots; orange-fleshed for sweetness and moisture, whiter Asian types for a denser, chestnut-like bite.

storage.text: Keep cool, dark, and dry — never the fridge, which toughens the core. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: root-vegetable storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Mash leftovers into pancakes or a quick soup with coconut milk.

substitutions.note: works in soups and roasts; less starch
